tests.covers: Production startup page with a simulated launcher: saved settings start the engine, loading and prefill phases, memory plan and context are shown, and readiness navigates to the app.
The activity animation runs without changing the shown percentage and stops under reduced motion.
Production startup function: with no engine running it reads status and posts one start with the default context.

cases.use: The user downloads a model from Settings: confirmation, engine preparation, transfer, verification and completion, without changing the selected model.

tests.covers: Real host and Settings controls with fixture installer and tiny weights: confirm, installing engine, downloading, verifying and completed, with the composer model label unchanged.
Real host /api/model/download with fixture installer and downloader: installing then downloading then verifying, complete only after the downloader exits, files published in the admitted store.
A non-default GGUF and a 27B MLX folder each install their engine first, receive their variant and store identity and complete at 100.

cases.use: A download fetches the pinned files (with the user's Hugging Face token when needed, never exposing it), verifies size and hash and publishes them under their final names.

tests.covers: Production downloader with real curl against a loopback server: a fresh transfer publishes exact bytes, removes the partial and verifies; a repeat makes no request. The token reaches HTTP as a Bearer header and never appears in the curl arguments.
Generic downloader CLI on a test catalog: single-file GGUF, a 27B GGUF with its projector, a split BF16 pair and an MLX folder with config.json last.

Production DeepSeek V4.1 shell downloader with real curl: each of the three pins is fetched from its revision URL and a rerun makes no request (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs under make test-ds41-1017-download). The token is sent as a Bearer header from the flag, the environment and the cache file (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).

cases.use: Download progress, paused state and Stop/Resume appear in Settings while the composer keeps showing the selected model.

tests.covers: Authored background download status: Settings shows 16%, 37% and paused with Stop or Resume enabled while the composer label stays, and no start or download request is issued.
Real host status counts the folder and its staging against the pinned 36.67 GB, stays below 100 while verifying and reaches 100 only on downloader exit.

cases.use: Downloading a vision-capable model automatically downloads its matching encoder afterwards.

tests.covers: Real host with fixture download scripts: GLM chains its encoder, V4.1 Q2 chains the 1017 sidecar and Q4 the original one; text-only and support files chain nothing.

cases.use: The user presses Open folder and the folder that receives the download opens.

tests.covers: Real host /api/model/folder/open runs the opener on the downloading store and refuses a model that is not downloading.

cases.use: The model list shows the models installed under every engine folder and offers every pinned variant with its label, size and required companion files, per platform.

tests.covers: Host catalog loader on the shipped file: 63 variants, compiled pins equal their entries and the endpoint serves the file byte for byte (make test-qwen-variants).
Production UI functions on the shipped catalog: one offer per pinned variant with labels and groups, and installed variants listed with quantization.
Production catalog functions for DeepSeek V4.1: Q2, Q4 and 1017 names, API ids and which download each file hides.
Real host /api/ggufs aggregates two checkouts, one through a symlinked store, with engine folder and branch per file.

cases.use: Switching between Agent, Cowork, Design and Chat keeps the same resident model process when the engine allows it.

tests.covers: Agent to Cowork to Design to Chat on a llama.cpp model keeps the same resident server pid.

cases.use: Each model file is routed to the engine that supports it: ds4, Laguna, llama.cpp or MLX.

tests.covers: Production routing functions: pinned Qwen GGUFs go to llama.cpp, the pinned MLX folder to MLX, and all four launch modes are supported for them (make test-resident-unit).
Production model classification: Flash-Next and 27B files, auxiliary sidecars and Qwen routing (make test-engine-setup-unit).

cases.use: The user downloads a model with download-model.sh; the engine is installed first and the files land in the right store.

tests.covers: Root download-model.sh with stub make and dstudio: a GGUF and an MLX target install their engine then land in ds4/gguf or the MLX folder; --list-qwen lists the catalog.
Root download-model.sh routes the three V4.1 pins to the pinned script and other targets to the engine script (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).

cases.use: Starting a download for files that are already complete only verifies them and keeps the selected model and engine untouched.

tests.covers: Real host with the full-size 27B weights and projector already installed: the download request verifies them to 100% without loading a model and leaves file identities unchanged.

cases.use: Each supported installed model is loaded in turn through the app and answers a checked prompt in the Chat UI.

tests.covers: Loads every supported installed model one at a time through the bundled app on the engine the app routes it to, asserts the engine process and memory mode, and checks arithmetic, JSON extraction and a Chat UI answer. Not yet run in its November 11 form.

cases.use: A model is usable only when all its parts are present in the same engine folder: projector, both halves of a split file, or the MLX folder.

tests.covers: Production rules: pinned 27B quantizations need the projector, split BF16 needs both parts in one folder and MLX 4-bit needs none.
Host recognition and preflight: second split parts and projectors are auxiliary and a missing part or projector is model_component_missing (make test-qwen-variants).
An MLX folder counts as present only with config.json, also through a symlink (make test-resident-unit).

cases.use: Encoders, drafters, partial files and unpublished or modified weights are not offered as models.

tests.covers: The picker lists eleven models and no engine-branch entry, support file, projector, unpinned 27B quantization or second split part.
Modified weights, Q3, .assembling and .part files are not selectable; the encoder is a component, not a model.

cases.use: The user types in the picker while the catalog is still loading or a download poll runs; typed text and focus are kept.

tests.covers: Typing with the catalog held keeps text and focus when rows arrive; a background download poll causes no rescan and no label change.

cases.use: The picker, composer controls and startup screen stay reachable on small and phone-sized windows in both themes.

tests.covers: At 1440, 390 and 320 px in dark and light the picker stays in the window near its button and all composer controls remain hit-testable.
At 360 by 740 and 320 by 480 the startup page has no sideways overflow and the metrics stay reachable.

cases.use: Loading or preparing a model takes hours; the attempt stays pending with Cancel available and is never timed out by the app.

tests.covers: With the start request held and the clock advanced an hour the request stays connected and status polling continues.
With the work clock advanced four hours the overlay and Cancel remain and no loading timeout appears.
Production owner ticks with the clock four hours ahead: a silent resident server, a launch preparation and a shared engine still loading stay running with no error (make test-slow-runtime).
The readiness waiter does not expire or relaunch across four simulated hours of loading.

cases.use: The user double-clicks a model, presses another mode shortcut, repeats a download request or many requests wait for the same model; only one launch or download is admitted and excess waiters are refused explicitly.

tests.covers: Two clicks in one event turn with status held, then Cancel: no launch and the saved model unchanged.
A second mode shortcut during the pending switch admits no second /api/start.
A duplicate /api/model/download while one is active answers 409.
During preparation a duplicate start and a web-directory change answer launch_busy.
Thirty-two observers are admitted and the thirty-third is refused "Too many requests"; aborting waiters leave the shared launch intact.

cases.use: Two downloader processes target the same file; one proceeds and the other is told it is already active.

tests.covers: A concurrent call during a blocked transfer fails "already active" with one HTTP request; the leader completes.
A second invocation while one download is held fails with "already active" (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).

cases.use: For models that do not support power throttling, SSD streaming or the largest contexts, those controls are disabled with an explanation.

tests.covers: On 27B the power and SSD controls are disabled with a reason and the 393,216 context option is disabled.
On Qwen the Performance pane disables power and SSD streaming with an "Unavailable for Qwen" notice that wraps at 390 px.

cases.use: A configuration that exceeds the memory budget is not started silently; the user sees the figures and must confirm.

tests.covers: An over-budget 409 opens the dialog with the required and available GiB; the engine is not started without confirmation.
Host context-memory bounds; with local weights present a 1M context over budget is refused without confirmation (make test-lan-unit).

cases.use: The user selects another engine folder or the store is a link while a download runs; the download stays bound to the store it was admitted for.

tests.covers: A checkout change mid-download leaves progress and downloader arguments on the original store and its identity.
A model folder that is a symlink is admitted by its target's identity and the file lands in the target.

cases.use: MLX downloads are offered only on a Mac; other platforms see only the llama.cpp variants.

tests.covers: A Mac offers the MLX download until the folder is listed; Linux, Windows and unknown platforms never do.
Off Apple Silicon the real host refuses the MLX target with 400 before any installer starts.

cases.use: When the engine reports another model or configuration, the memory and prefill figures of the previous one are cleared.

tests.covers: A changed model file or configuration resets memory and prefill to a dash and unknown first counters show a dash.

cases.use: The disk fills up or has too little free space for a download; the download stops with a clear message and a resumable partial.

tests.covers: The production page, host and Qwen downloader with real curl fill a task-owned HFS+ volume: the toast names "No space left on device", the byte-exact partial is shown as Paused, and Resume after freeing space continues with an HTTP range from a loopback Hugging Face fixture.

cases.use: With SSD expert streaming and a large context, prompts whose batches select many different experts are prefilled correctly.

tests.covers: Real DeepSeek weights, first transformer layer only, 131,072 context with SSD streaming: outputs for 1 to 1,024 tokens equal the upstream reference bit for bit and the legacy build reproduces the 139-token failure. Not a full-model run.

cases.use: A downloaded file has the wrong size or checksum; it is not published and the user is told.

tests.covers: A corrupted stream gives "Checksum mismatch" with no final file; a wrong existing final file fails untouched with zero requests (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).
A full-size wrong partial reports a checksum mismatch and is not published; oversized bodies are refused.
A failing verification leaves the host phase failed with a paused variant and the partial kept.

A copy of the engine's download script with tiny size and hash literals and a stub transport: a truncated or altered existing file is rejected with "Incorrect file size" or "Checksum mismatch" and the model link is unchanged.

cases.use: The server answers with an error, ignores resume ranges or redirects somewhere unsafe; the download fails and the partial is preserved.

tests.covers: HTTP 503 and a server ignoring Range both fail with the partial unchanged and nothing published (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).
HTTP 404, an ignored Range and a redirect to a file URL fail with nothing published.

cases.use: A download is requested for a target that is not pinned in the catalog; it is refused before anything starts.

tests.covers: Real host answers 400 for an unpinned target before any child process starts.
The downloader exits 2 for an unknown variant and the shell wrapper stops before building.

cases.use: Preparing the engine for a model fails; the download is marked failed and no weights are transferred.

tests.covers: An installer exiting 9 leaves the phase failed and the weight downloader never starts.
A failing MLX installer leaves the phase failed with no weight transfer.

cases.use: A partial file or the store is a link, oversized, not private or was replaced; the downloader refuses to write.

tests.covers: Symlinked target, partial or lock, hard-linked or oversized partial, non-private stage and a replaced store are all refused with files untouched.
Symlinked and oversized partials are refused with zero requests (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).
The real downloader in verify-only mode rejects a folder replaced after admission.

cases.use: A launch names a missing model file or an option the model does not support (SSD streaming, throttled power, speculation, context); it is refused with a code and nothing changes.

tests.covers: Real start handler, 31 refusals: each returns its code and leaves mode, model, configuration, credentials, task counters and the running stand-in engine untouched (make test-launch-preflight).
Preflight for llama.cpp and MLX models refuses throttled power, speculation, over-large context and SSD streaming (make test-resident-unit).
Through the real host, before any model is loaded, Agent and Cowork starts with SSD streaming on for the Qwen model answer 409 unsupported_memory_mode.

cases.use: The engine folder is unavailable, memory cannot be allocated, the port is taken or preparation fails; the error is shown in front and stays readable.

tests.covers: A checkout 409 and a start 409 each show their message in front with the loading overlay hidden.
A launch_prepare_failed reply stays readable after 30 seconds and "Open DStudio" still works.
An occupied engine port returns false with the launcher's message and no forced retry.
A status carrying an engine error shows the error text on the startup screen and "Open DStudio" still opens the app.

cases.use: The model catalog cannot be refreshed; the picker says so.

tests.covers: A 503 from the catalog shows "Could not refresh models".

cases.use: Abliterated, uncensored or otherwise modified weights and unknown file names are not accepted as supported models.

tests.covers: Host model classification refuses derivative GGUF names (make test-engine-setup-unit).
Unpublished, abliterated and traversal names are refused; an invalid catalog edit is rejected whole (make test-qwen-variants).

cases.use: The model file or its encoder changes while the launch is being prepared; the launch is refused as stale.

tests.covers: Checkpoint bytes changed or an encoder appearing during a blocked build give launch_stale with state unchanged and the old engine still answering.

Only the capture step: the production function records model, projector and installer-script dependencies of three launches within its fixed bound; revalidation is not executed here (make test-launch-dependencies).

cases.use: Another model, build or context answers the readiness probe; the launch is not declared ready.

tests.covers: llama.cpp /props and MLX /v1/models readiness: any mismatch of path, alias, build, slots, context or vision is not ready (make test-resident-unit).
Another model or the same file from another engine folder is not treated as ready; a launch that comes up at the wrong context is rejected.

cases.use: The model server executable changed after it was checked, or the engine is being installed; the server is not started.

tests.covers: Real guard process: an edited executable exits 126 unexecuted and a held install lock exits 125 within two seconds.

cases.use: The user asks to delete partial files that live in a locked, resumable download cache; the host refuses and keeps them.

tests.covers: Real host /api/model/partials/delete for the paused pinned download answers 409 and the 4,096-byte partial and completed file stay.
The handler called directly for a V4.1 target answers 409 Conflict with the partial bytes still present (make test-qwen27-download-host).

cases.use: A download is interrupted by a dropped connection or the app quitting; the next attempt resumes from the exact partial size.

tests.covers: A connection cut after 1 MiB is retried with the exact Range, and an existing partial is adopted in place and resumed (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).
A 137-byte partial resumes with Range 137-; a transfer truncated at 123 bytes keeps the partial and the rerun resumes from it.

cases.use: The user stops a download and later resumes it to completion.

tests.covers: Stop shows Paused with Resume enabled; Resume completes and both fixture files exist with the expected bytes.
SIGTERM to the downloader keeps the partial with no final file and the rerun resumes at the exact size (started by tests/integration/ds41_1017_download_test.mjs).
SIGTERM during a blocked transfer exits 130 with the curl child gone; the rerun completes.
Stop during the model or the encoder phase ends as stopped; the model file is kept and the encoder absent.

cases.use: After the app restarts, a partially downloaded model is shown as paused with its bytes.

tests.covers: Host progress accounting on partial files; after download state is cleared an orphan partial is found as paused (make test-qwen27-download-host).
After globals are cleared a staged part, a projector-only state and an MLX stage are found as paused (make test-qwen-variants).
After a page reload the paused transfer is shown again in Settings.

cases.use: After a failed download the user starts it again and it completes.

tests.covers: A new /api/model/download after the failed verification completes at 100 with the original selection unchanged; reuse of the kept partial is not asserted.

cases.use: The user cancels a model that is loading; the attempt ends, processes are reaped and the previous conversation and settings are intact.

tests.covers: Cancel posts the task id and hides the overlay with the saved chat and settings unchanged; a pending launch of another window offers no Cancel.
Real host: cancel with the right task id during preparation or loading ends as launch_canceled, reaps builder and engine and ignores late readiness.
Launch cancel reaps the worker; a cancel with the wrong task id is refused and a shared engine stays alive (make test-slow-runtime).

cases.use: While a new model is being prepared the previous engine still reports ready; the new attempt is not shown as finished.

tests.covers: With a pending preparation an old ready engine leaves the percentage unknown and the page in place.
A launch accepted while status still reports the old ready model keeps the overlay at 0 until the new one loads.

cases.use: After a failed launch the user tries again and the new attempt is admitted cleanly.

tests.covers: After a visible launch error a new launch is admitted and its overlay outlives the old error timer.
Confirming the over-budget dialog retries exactly once with the override and then opens the app.

cases.use: The saved engine folder or model is stale at startup; it is repaired from the catalog or replaced by what is actually running.

tests.covers: A stale saved engine folder is repaired with a checkout request before the start.
After reload with a Flash status the stale saved Pro model is replaced and shown.
An unlisted active checkout is corrected with a checkout request before exactly one start.

cases.use: After a failed refresh or a missing catalog file the model list works again.

tests.covers: With the catalog back the rows return.
Without the catalog file the host serves the three original pins; pointing back restores the full catalog byte for byte.

cases.use: The app quits, crashes or stops the model; the model server does not stay behind holding memory.

tests.covers: After the host is killed the real llama.cpp or MLX server is gone within ten seconds.
Real guard process: closing the owner channel stops the server and one ignoring SIGTERM is killed after the grace period.
Killing the host during preparation ends builder and worker; stopping a TERM-ignoring engine still completes.

cases.use: The user switches model and switches back while a launch or request is pending; the stale work is discarded and the current selection wins.

tests.covers: An A to B to A selection during pending status rejects the stale waiter with zero starts.
After a repair an A to B to A selection makes the stale request fail with nothing sent.

cases.use: The user deletes the partial files of a stopped download to free disk space and the bytes are removed.

tests.covers: Delete partial in Settings -> Models (refused while the download runs, confirmed in a dialog) removes a stopped ds4 .part and the Laguna cache partials through the real host; the volume regains exactly those bytes and the completed model is untouched.

cases.use: The user opens Settings, moves between panes and searches for an option.

tests.covers: Production Settings dialog with an authored launcher: navigation groups, the Connection pane with engine state, the Models pane and a search for "wired limit" that jumps to Performance.
With the history collapsed the Settings dialog still opens and closes from the rail.

cases.use: The user chooses Light, Dark or System; the page and the native window follow.

tests.covers: Light is chosen in Settings, Interface and the same layout checks pass; Dark is selected again.
On the real host page the theme radio sets the page theme attribute.
With theme System the startup page follows the emulated OS scheme and posts the theme to the native handler stub.
A real Cocoa window with the production wrapper: light and dark theme messages set the window background and appearance (make test-macos-window-theme).

cases.use: On launch the saved theme is already applied before the app has loaded its history.

tests.covers: With the history database held open forever, the inert page already carries the saved or system theme and a matching rail colour.

cases.use: The user changes the context size; a restart is confirmed and the next start uses the new size.

tests.covers: Choosing 16,384 and "Restart now" posts /api/start with the same model and the new context.
Choosing 65,536 opens the restart confirmation; Cancel closes Settings and the value still reads 65,536 afterwards.

cases.use: The user picks a thinking level in the composer and it is saved for that mode.

tests.covers: In Agent the selector persists off and then high in the saved settings.
The composer pill reads "Thinking: high" and the max item states its context requirement.

cases.use: The user sets page-read and candidate limits for Search and Deep Research.

tests.covers: Settings, Web research shows 8/96/24/256, accepts new values, persists them and keeps them after reload.

cases.use: The user sets the image preset and the video duration, aspect and profile; later requests use them.

tests.covers: Each image preset is persisted without restarting the engine.
Settings, Video shows the saved duration and aspect and the generate request uses them.
Production preset selector keeps low, medium, high and max and falls back to max for unknown values.

cases.use: The user changes the GPU wired-memory limit and advanced engine toggles.

tests.covers: A wired limit of 94,112 is posted to the (fixture) endpoint with a success message; the Advanced pane shows its toggles and installed drafters.

cases.use: Sidebar collapse, IDE layout and divider position are remembered.

tests.covers: A collapsed sidebar is saved and stays collapsed after reload.
The IDE layout and divider position are persisted and applied.

cases.use: On launch the saved model, context, power and SSD preferences are sent to the launcher.

tests.covers: The start request carries the saved model file, context 131,072, power 70 and SSD off; three models by three SSD preferences each send one start with the model-appropriate value.
Production launch-base function returns the saved context, power and SSD choice without mutating settings.

cases.use: Options that a model cannot use are overridden only for that launch; the saved preferences for other models stay.

tests.covers: A 27B launch uses power 100 and SSD off while saved power 90, SSD on and drafter preferences are untouched.
After loading Qwen the saved DeepSeek power 90 and SSD on are still stored.

cases.use: The host remembers its HTTP port and the selected engine folder across launches, and honours a custom data folder.

tests.covers: Host functions write the http-port file and round-trip an engine folder path containing a space (make test-lan-unit).
An explicit data directory moves the history store path, and a KV directory override is honoured (make test-engine-setup-unit).

cases.use: The user opens diagnostics to see runtime state, recent tasks and error logs.

tests.covers: Real host diagnostics, logs and tasks endpoints return their documented shapes, and a failed send appears as a failed task with its error log.

cases.use: Selecting Thinking: max below the required context explains the memory cost; Cancel changes nothing and Confirm raises the context and restarts once.

tests.covers: The dialog names 384k, the current 64k and the RAM; Cancel sends no start; Confirm stores 393,216 with exactly one start; re-selecting max still warns.
On 27B selecting Max asks one loop warning with no context wording and declining keeps the level and context.

cases.use: A field in a pane the user is not looking at holds an invalid value; Done still closes Settings and nothing is restarted.

tests.covers: With a step-mismatched wired limit in a hidden pane, Done and the close button still close the dialog with no start request.

cases.use: The saved theme value is unknown or the settings were written by another schema version; defaults are used.

tests.covers: An unknown theme gives dark; another schema version and missing settings give the default light.

cases.use: Settings and the composer menus fit a phone-sized window.

tests.covers: In the light theme at 390 by 844 the dialog stays inside the window with its section navigation visible.
The gear popover and its dropdown lie inside the window and Escape leaves no detached menu.

cases.use: A profile saved by an older version (old quality defaults) is migrated on load.

tests.covers: A legacy profile at max with context 131,072 keeps max, shows the context hint and moves the defaults version from 1 to 2.

cases.use: The preferred HTTP port is taken; the host opens the next free one.

tests.covers: The listener function moves to the next port when the first is taken (make test-lan-unit).

cases.use: The saved settings are damaged (invalid JSON); the app starts with defaults instead of failing.

tests.covers: Damaged settings JSON still yields a themed, inert first paint with the default light theme and no page error.

cases.use: A stored preference holds an out-of-range or invalid value; it is ignored in favour of the default.

tests.covers: Invalid stored research limits and values above the maximum fall back to the defaults.
The host configuration parser rejects an unsupported model value (make test-lan-unit).

cases.use: Browser storage refuses a settings write; the user is told the engine started but the settings need attention.

tests.covers: With setItem throwing a quota error after an adjusted start, no second start happens and the message names browser storage.

cases.use: A launch is rejected; the active configuration and stored preferences are exactly as before.

tests.covers: Every refused start leaves configuration, credentials, memory settings and task counters unchanged (make test-launch-preflight).
Rejected Design starts leave /api/status fields and the task list unchanged.

cases.use: While a context or Max confirmation is open the model or context changes; the stale confirmation is not applied.

tests.covers: A pending Max confirmation is rejected after a model switch, a context change or an A to B to A switch.

cases.use: A host-side preference file (engine folder, port) is damaged or points nowhere; the host starts and reports the problem.

tests.covers: Real host startup with an engine-folder preference that points nowhere, names a file or holds damaged bytes: status and the doctor check report the folder as unusable, the file is left unchanged and the host exits cleanly. The http-port file, read only by the windowed launcher, is not executed.

cases.use: Changed settings are still there after a reload.

tests.covers: The changed web research limits survive a reload.
The collapsed state survives a reload and Expand restores the list.

cases.use: The user cancels a launch; model, context, SSD and folder settings are unchanged.

tests.covers: After Cancel the saved model, variant, context, SSD and workdir settings are unchanged.

cases.use: The user leaves Thinking: max; the context returns to what it was before.

tests.covers: Choosing high from max and confirming restores context 65,536 and clears the remembered value.

cases.use: The launcher lowers a requested value (context, drafter); the adjusted value is written back so the UI shows what is really used.

tests.covers: An adjusted reply with context 65,536 and drafter off is written back to the saved settings.

cases.use: The browser storage quota is exhausted by history; settings can still be changed and saved.

tests.covers: After a 6 MiB history moves to IndexedDB the theme setting still saves, and it stays writable while the native store is read-only.

areas.label: Saved conversations, sessions, history and reopening

cases.use: Every message, including text still streaming, is saved to history as the conversation grows.

tests.covers: In all five modes the saved answer or transcript equals every byte of the authored stream, protocol events included for the native modes.
Production native store: a save is acknowledged durable with a new revision and the file bytes equal the body (make test-chat-store-unit).

cases.use: Chat, Agent, Cowork, Design and Learn each keep their own reopenable history.

tests.covers: Production store code with real IndexedDB and the real host file: five modes saved with long reasoning, native transcripts and a Tutor thread are all kept in the native file.

cases.use: The user clicks another conversation in the sidebar and it opens.

tests.covers: Clicking the second row switches the header title to that conversation.

cases.use: The user pins a conversation and it moves under Pinned.

tests.covers: Conversation actions, Pin puts the row under a Pinned label.

cases.use: The user renames a conversation; the sidebar, header and saved title change.

tests.covers: Rename plus Enter updates the row, the saved chat title and the header.
A roadmap chat is renamed through the sidebar actions.

cases.use: The user starts a new conversation from the header.

tests.covers: The header New chat control sets the title to "New chat".

cases.use: The user deletes one conversation and it disappears from history.

tests.covers: Delete from the row menu removes one conversation from the sidebar, the browser history and the host store with a tombstone; the other conversations are unchanged and it stays deleted after a reload.

cases.use: The user clears all history; conversations are gone everywhere and stay gone.

tests.covers: clearAll leaves no chats with content and an older window's later save does not bring them back.
The native wipe leaves an empty chat list in memory and on disk (make test-chat-store-unit).

cases.use: The user collapses the history panel; the mode rail and Settings stay available.

tests.covers: Collapsed, the sidebar is 80 px with the list hidden and all five mode tabs visible.

cases.use: In Agent, Cowork and Design the user saves, lists, switches to and deletes runtime sessions.

tests.covers: Built Agent binary run as Agent and as Cowork: a session is saved, listed with its first prompt and deleted.
Built Design runtime: /list reports the current session and /del removes its file.
Clicking the /list hint in Cowork sends the command through the runtime.

cases.use: A real Cowork or Design run leaves its on-disk session so it can be reopened.

tests.covers: After the real run the Cowork KV cache holds the system-prompt file and a session file.
After the real run the Design session folder holds a session file.

cases.use: The runtime's "saved session" note appears as a service line, not as part of the model's answer.

tests.covers: The production transcript segmenter turns the autosave receipt into a system segment and the visible text equals the answer.

cases.use: History grows beyond the small browser quota (megabytes of reasoning and transcripts); it moves to IndexedDB without losing text.

tests.covers: A 6 MiB Chat message is kept in the native file and IndexedDB and the localStorage chat key is removed.
An 8 MiB body is saved durably and reloaded identically (make test-chat-store-unit).

cases.use: Several saves are requested while one is still being written; one write is in flight and later saves still complete.

tests.covers: Three saves with the first native write gated: one write in flight and all three promises resolve.
While the writer is blocked at the publish barrier a read answers and a second save or wipe gets store_busy (make test-chat-store-unit).

cases.use: The browser database is busy; a save still succeeds once the native file acknowledges it.

tests.covers: With an IndexedDB transaction held open the save resolves after the native durable acknowledgement.

cases.use: Two windows edit different conversations; both sets of changes are merged, and a conversation being streamed in one window is not overwritten by the other.

tests.covers: Two pages edit different chats and both are in the native file; a streaming chat with a remote edit refuses to save and keeps its local value.

cases.use: On a phone-sized window the conversations menu slides in and nothing overflows.

tests.covers: At 390 by 740 the conversations menu opens the sidebar with no horizontal overflow.

cases.use: In the desktop app the main window, the Learn study room and the Design canvas keep their controls out of the native title-bar strip, and pane colours run to the top.

tests.covers: Screenshot pixels in the top inset continue each pane's colour in both themes.
With a simulated 28 px inset no operable main-window control intersects the strip. With a simulated 28 px inset no operable control of the study room intersects the strip and its header covers it.
With a simulated 28 px title-bar inset the canvas and full-screen bars cover the strip and hold no control inside it.

cases.use: The user changes mode or view while a session command is pending; the command is cancelled and nothing is rebound.

tests.covers: A view change or a switch to Design while awaiting the transcript cancels new, save and switch with no command sent.

cases.use: History reaches the 64 MiB save limit or more than 64 pending save callers; the excess is refused explicitly and nothing is trimmed.

tests.covers: Production Store refuses a history over 64 MiB and a 65th pending save caller with explicit messages while memory, the browser copy and the native file keep every byte; the real host saves exactly 64 MiB, answers 413 to one byte more and reloads the whole file after a restart.

cases.use: A new session is requested while a session list is still in flight; the commands are ordered and the session is bound to the right conversation.

tests.covers: A new design during an in-flight list is ordered after it with no restart and the session id binds to the requesting conversation.

cases.use: The profile folder is read-only; the save falls back to the browser copy with a visible notice and the native file is not corrupted.

tests.covers: With the profile directory read-only the save succeeds browser-only with a "saved in this browser" notice and the native file is unchanged.
An injected write failure answers store_write_failed and file, revision and memory keep the previous content (make test-chat-store-unit).

cases.use: Both the native file and the browser store fail; the save reports failure and the conversation stays in memory.

tests.covers: With native and IndexedDB writes both denied the save returns false with a message and the in-memory reasoning and transcript are retained.

cases.use: A save arrives with a stale revision, a malformed revision header or invalid JSON; it is rejected and the stored history is unchanged.

tests.covers: A stale revision answers store_conflict and invalid JSON store_invalid with file and revision unchanged (make test-chat-store-unit).
Five malformed revision headers sent to the real host get 400 and the store is unchanged.

cases.use: The file was replaced but syncing the folder failed; the save is reported as uncertain and memory matches what is on disk.

tests.covers: An injected directory-sync failure answers store_durability_unknown with file and memory holding the new content (make test-chat-store-unit).

cases.use: A history write arrives without the app's request header; it is refused.

tests.covers: POST /api/store without the request header gets 403 from the real host.

cases.use: A saved session file is damaged; switching to it restores nothing and the live conversation continues.

tests.covers: A session file truncated by 20 bytes makes /switch fail with "nothing restored" and the live conversation is intact in the next request.
A Design session file truncated by 40 bytes restores nothing and the live conversation is kept.

cases.use: A conversation that holds only status bookkeeping or blank notices is treated as empty rather than shown as content.

tests.covers: Production predicates return false for sessions or status bookkeeping, a blank notice and a non-string notice.

cases.use: The app is quit and started again; all conversations are restored from the host file.

tests.covers: The real host is stopped and restarted: a new page restores all five modes and the 6 MiB body, and the old page saves again after the revision reset.
After memory is cleared the store load restores identical bytes from the file (make test-chat-store-unit).
With a custom data directory a written store file is loaded back at revision 1 (make test-engine-setup-unit).

cases.use: The browser profile is empty but the host has the history; the conversation is restored from the host.

tests.covers: A fresh browser context with empty local history restores the conversation from the store reply of the mock server (not the native host).

cases.use: A store that refused writes works again; the next save succeeds and the native file catches up with what was saved in the browser.

tests.covers: After permissions are restored the native file contains the change saved browser-only before. After both stores were denied a later save succeeds.

cases.use: The Agent, Cowork or Design runtime is restarted; the saved session is restored and continues with the same conversation.

tests.covers: After a kill a new process switches to the saved session and resends the previous conversation unchanged plus the new line.
Real model: stop, start and switch to the saved Cowork session, then a follow-up recalls earlier facts.

cases.use: A new session is interrupted while it is being prepared; the old session, its memory and attachments remain.

tests.covers: An interrupt during the blocked prefill, also at the moment it returns success, keeps the old session and publishes no candidate.

Real Qwen weights on Metal through the engine session API: a candidate prefill cancelled before or during the first layers leaves the live session snapshot unchanged, and an uncancelled one equals a normal sync bit for bit.

cases.use: The user reloads the page; the open conversation, its attachments and its canvas come back.

tests.covers: A saved completed Design chat reopens its canvas and board after reload.
After reload the image gallery of the saved message is restored as previews.

cases.use: A reopened conversation returns to the reading position it had.

tests.covers: The production scroll controller restores a requested reading position across two frames after a rebuild.

areas.label: Stop, adding context while a turn runs, Goals and resuming

cases.use: The user presses Stop during a Chat answer; generation ends, the partial text is kept and the engine connection is closed.

tests.covers: Stop on a held authored stream saves the partial text with finishReason aborted.
On an already running host with real weights: Send, the Stop button appears and is clicked, and Send returns. The reply content is not graded.
Real host relay: a client abort while the engine is blocked resets the engine connection and the next request succeeds.
A client disconnect before response headers gives the engine socket a reset, not a silent close (make test-v1-relay).
Stop pressed by the corpus run loop during a held answer: the partial text is kept with finishReason aborted, the scripted engine sees its connection closed, and the question is not asked again.

cases.use: The user presses Stop while Agent, Cowork or Design waits for the model; the turn ends, the runtime goes back to waiting and the model request is closed.

tests.covers: Built Agent, Cowork and Design binaries receive an interrupt during a silent prefill and return to waiting within two seconds (started by tests/integration/agent_native_build_test.mjs under make test-agent-native-build).

Host Stop handler with a real child and a held connection through the model worker: Stop answers 200, the reader returns, the connection closes and the worker is reaped, for three modes and both protocols (make test-model-rpc-interrupt).
On a running host with real weights each of Agent, Cowork and Design accepts a prompt, is stopped from the UI and returns to idle.
Real Laguna weights: an interrupt after at least 32 generated tokens prints "Stopped by user" and the process stays alive.

cases.use: After Stop the conversation shows a "Stopped by user" service line, not raw protocol text, and the composer is usable.

tests.covers: An authored runtime notice shows as a service segment with no JSON and the composer enabled, in Agent and Cowork.
The production segmenter renders a notice frame at every split point without leaking the frame and keeps plain prose saying the same words as text.
The patched worker emits a byte-exact "Stopped by user" notice frame.

cases.use: The user sends another message while a Chat answer is streaming; the partial answer is kept and the next request continues with the new text.

tests.covers: A message sent during an open Chat stream produces a request with the partial assistant text, one original user turn and the new text last.

cases.use: In Agent, Cowork or Design the user sends text while a turn runs; it is added to the current turn at the next boundary without stopping it or repeating a tool.

tests.covers: Sending during a working turn posts /api/agent/steer with the turn id, no new send or interrupt, and the applied receipt clears the queue.
Production host steering handler and runtime client: input admitted for the active turn, delivered to the worker, marked applied with a receipt (make test-steering).
Built Agent, Cowork and Design binaries: context queued during round one appears in the next model request together with the real tool result, and the tool ran once.

cases.use: In a Tutor room the user sends a follow-up while the reply streams; the next request keeps the partial reply and the attachment.

tests.covers: A Tutor message sent mid-stream produces a request with the partial assistant text, the new message once and the attachment.

cases.use: The user sets /goal; the Agent keeps taking turns until a verification command succeeds and a completion receipt is given.

tests.covers: Production Goal scheduler and journal with fixture transcript frames: a turn without completion starts attempt two as a continuation, and completion plus a successful check ends the graph as succeeded (make test-goal).
Typing /goal sends the goal orchestration flag.

cases.use: The user pauses, resumes and clears a goal with the buttons or commands.

tests.covers: Pause, typed /goal resume and Clear call the pause, resume and cancel endpoints with the graph id and sequence and send no model prompt.
Pause during a running turn ends paused after it; resume dispatches the next attempt (make test-goal).

cases.use: In a GSA/RSA run the user pauses, advances one phase and resumes.

tests.covers: Pause holds after the current save, Next phase admits exactly one turn and Resume runs the remaining phases in order.

cases.use: The user stops a running GSA/RSA turn; one interrupt is sent, earlier artifacts are kept and the step is marked incomplete.

tests.covers: Stop during an active RSA turn sends one interrupt, shows stopped and keeps the earlier report and inventory.

cases.use: The user stops a turn run by pi or OpenCode; the in-flight model request fails and the harness returns to waiting.

tests.covers: Bridge classes with a fake pi: abort during a running turn ends with a second waiting marker and no turn-error marker; cancelAll fails in-flight and queued requests.

cases.use: Stopping the model stops its server process and resets a request in flight to it.

tests.covers: A request to the owned resident endpoint stays live while silent; Stop resets its socket and only the worker is reaped (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).
A resident stop request reaps the child within three seconds (make test-slow-runtime).

cases.use: Stop arrives before the first token, in the middle of a frame or after an uncommitted tool call; nothing of the cancelled work appears or runs.

tests.covers: Interrupt after an unfinished delta leaves no inherited bytes in the next prompt and an uncommitted bash call never creates its file (started by tests/integration/agent_native_build_test.mjs under make test-agent-native-build).
A pre-aborted stream performs no fetch; headers arriving after an abort are never read; buffered frames after an abort are not delivered.
Stop between two request-header fragments admits nothing and leaves the transcript empty (cases in model_rpc_input_test.c).

cases.use: Stop is pressed while the runtime is not reading, an upload is stalled or a helper is frozen; the Stop request still returns promptly.

tests.covers: With a frozen helper and a saturated pipe, Stop answers 200 and the old worker is reaped before the next request reaches the network (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).
With the upload worker frozen the HTTP Stop handler answers in under a second and the blocked worker is reaped (cases in model_rpc_input_test.c).

cases.use: A model request is queued or a tool batch is pending when Stop arrives; it is discarded, not started.

tests.covers: With an interrupt pending, a queued model request creates no worker (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).
An interrupt control frame after a tool batch returns the stop code with no calls.
A queued tool-call candidate is discarded on Stop and descriptor flags are restored (make test-model-rpc-interrupt).

cases.use: A goal runs up to its turn budget and a single turn may last hours; it is never cut by elapsed time and stops for input at the budget.

tests.covers: A running Goal turn survives a four-hour scheduler tick with no retry; at the two-turn budget the goal needs input and resume is refused (make test-goal).

cases.use: The user sends many context messages or the same one twice; they are queued in order up to a limit and duplicates are applied once.

tests.covers: Sixteen inputs are accepted and the seventeenth gets 429; a repeated input id stays one entry; pending inputs are delivered first-in first-out (make test-steering).

cases.use: Context arrives just as the turn would end; the turn continues for one more round instead of dropping it.

tests.covers: Context queued at the final boundary forces a third model round in the same turn.
A finish boundary with pending inputs keeps the turn open and the next finish seals it (make test-steering).

cases.use: Stop or Pause is pressed while a workflow phase or its start is being saved; the save settles, nothing further is sent and saved effects are kept.

tests.covers: Stop while a phase save or the start reply is held: no further send, the saved inventory is kept and a late prepared prompt is never sent.

cases.use: Stop arrives while the session is being compacted, saved or reset; the pending change is not published and the old state remains.

tests.covers: An interrupt during blocked summary or rebuild, also at the instant the session call succeeds, publishes no candidate.
An interrupt during a deferred operation is latched while status stays readable.

cases.use: The model claims the goal is done without a successful verification command, or fakes success for a failed command; the goal is not completed.

tests.covers: A completion marker without tool evidence or with a failed command spoofing success ends as needs-input; receipts with interrupted, timed-out or failing commands are rejected (make test-goal).

cases.use: Context is sent for a turn that already ended, another turn, or while Stop is pending; it is refused.

tests.covers: A stale turn id gets 409, a malformed one 400, input after the turn is sealed 409 and input while an interrupt is pending 409 (make test-steering).

cases.use: The process relaying a model request crashes or cannot connect; the runtime receives an error, never a fake completion.

tests.covers: A killed helper and an unreachable endpoint each produce a model error and no completion (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).

cases.use: The app is killed while a model request is in flight; the helper process and its connection do not survive.

tests.covers: With the owning host killed, the helper's held connection closes and its process group empties.

cases.use: A turn ends with a runtime error while a goal is active; the goal waits for input instead of retrying blindly.

tests.covers: A turn-error marker before the waiting marker ends as needs-input with the attempt count unchanged (make test-goal).

cases.use: A reply or tool result arrives after the user stopped; it does not change the conversation.

tests.covers: A late extractor reply after Stop leaves the stored chat identical.
A late frame of a cancelled request id is not delivered.
A late response queued before cancel never reaches the runtime pipe (make test-slow-runtime).

cases.use: The watchdog or a Task Graph cancel ends a turn that is waiting on the model; the request is closed the same way as Stop.

tests.covers: Task Graph cancel and a watchdog trip each wake the reader, close the held connection and reap the worker (make test-model-rpc-interrupt).

cases.use: After Stop the user sends a new prompt; the same runtime process answers and tools work, with no leftovers from the stopped turn.

tests.covers: The same process runs the next turn: a real tool executes, its result reaches the model and exactly three requests were made (started by tests/integration/agent_native_build_test.mjs under make test-agent-native-build).
Real weights: after the stop the same process writes and reads recovered.txt and the earlier output file is unchanged.
The built Design runtime, interrupted with the stream open, takes a second prompt and reports "resumed successfully".
After an interrupt during an unfinished batch or a running shell command the next turn's write runs and history shows the tool as interrupted.

cases.use: The user stops Cowork mid-task and asks it to continue; the task finishes with a single correct output.

tests.covers: Real model: interrupted after the first tool result and resumed in the same session, the status report is correct and unique.

cases.use: Context queued for an interrupted turn is not replayed on its own; it stays visible until the user sends or dismisses it.

tests.covers: A seeded pending context from an interrupted turn stays in the follow-up queue, persists unchanged and Dismiss removes it.

cases.use: A goal that paused or reported a blocker is resumed and completes with evidence.

tests.covers: A blocked marker ends as needs-input; resume starts attempt two and an evidence-backed completion succeeds (make test-goal).

cases.use: The app crashes while a goal turn runs or right after a resume was recorded; on reload nothing is dispatched twice and the goal waits for an explicit resume.

tests.covers: Reload after a crash during a running turn gives needs-input with one attempt; reload after a durable resume request dispatches nothing until resumed (make test-goal).

cases.use: A long reply is compacted mid-way; it continues from where it was and a Stop during that keeps the unfinished answer.

tests.covers: Scripted loop: Stop before dispatch generates nothing and Stop during rebuild keeps the incomplete answer.
Real weights: generation crosses a compaction without renewing the output budget and the result compiles and runs.

cases.use: After cancelling an image or video job the next Chat message is answered normally.

tests.covers: Stop during a held image request sends one stop for the same job and shows "Video generation cancelled"; the next Chat message gets its reply.

areas.label: pi and OpenCode as the Agent loop

cases.use: The user chooses pi or OpenCode as the Agent harness in Settings and the choice is saved and used for the next Agent start.

tests.covers: The Harness pane lists pi as installed and OpenCode as not installed; selecting pi persists agentHarness.
Every Agent /api/start body carries the saved harness opencode.

cases.use: The user installs a missing harness from Settings.

tests.covers: Install posts the harness name to a fixture endpoint and the installed one shows Reinstall; nothing is built.
Production installer functions on private copies: every listed patch applies with real git apply and the bundled snapshots verify byte for byte.

cases.use: With pi or OpenCode selected, the user gives the Agent a file task; the harness reads, computes and writes the file with the local model.

tests.covers: Real weights through the production host and bridge for pi and OpenCode: a CSV of random rows is read and total.txt equals an independently computed total with at least one tool call.
Bridge classes spawn a fake pi and a fake OpenCode: launch arguments and config are written and a prompt yields reasoning, tool call, tool result, text and the waiting marker.

cases.use: A second question in the same harness session is answered from what was read before.

tests.covers: Same session: the visible reply contains the random build code from the notes file.

cases.use: The harness's answer appears incrementally in the transcript.

tests.covers: Real weights with harness pi and opencode: the visible transcript grows in at least five increments, none larger than half.

cases.use: Tool calls from pi and OpenCode show as DStudio diff and command cards, with the file content previewed while it is generated.

tests.covers: Tool arguments of both harnesses map to diff and command cards; tool fragments stream to the harness and pi's tool-call events drive the preview before execution.

cases.use: The harness talks to the model DStudio selected, with its sampling and thinking rules, through a private local endpoint.

tests.covers: The loopback endpoint turns a request into one model request with the admitted model, kept temperature and the model family's thinking fields, for Qwen, remote and ds4 kinds.
The host start with a harness and a given model reaches ready and idle for each harness and model combination.

cases.use: Prompts and control frames reach the harness intact when they arrive in pieces or contain multibyte characters.

tests.covers: Host input class: a control frame is dispatched at once, a prompt after the quiet interval (30 ms in the test), a cut frame yields nothing and a split euro sign survives.

cases.use: The harness issues several model requests at once; they reach the model one at a time.

tests.covers: Two concurrent requests are forwarded to the host one at a time.

cases.use: A harness tool returns a very large result; it is truncated for display without breaking the transcript.

tests.covers: A 70 KiB tool result is truncated and frame order is kept.

cases.use: Tool-call fragments are cut at arbitrary byte positions; the preview and the final call are the same.

tests.covers: Write, edit, read and bash arguments at every three-way split give the same frames, and ds4-server fragments are extracted identically for every seven-byte cut.

cases.use: The harness is asked to read a file outside the working folder; the outside content does not come back.

tests.covers: Asked for a file outside the workspace, no read tool result contains the outside secret; the check also passes when no read is attempted.

cases.use: Session save, list and switch commands are not offered where the harness or model cannot support them.

tests.covers: The production command list hides save, list, switch and delete for Qwen with pi or OpenCode and keeps new, compact and help.

cases.use: Model or tool text contains characters that look like host protocol frames; it cannot forge an event.

tests.covers: Record and unit separators in model text cannot forge frames in the host output class.

cases.use: The validated tool call differs from what was streamed to the harness; the turn fails instead of running a different call.

tests.covers: A validated batch that differs from the streamed fragments yields "differs from the validated call" and no completion.

cases.use: Another local process calls the harness endpoint without the right key; it is refused.

tests.covers: A wrong bearer token gets 401 from the loopback endpoint.

cases.use: A bundled harness source drifted or a patch was already applied; installation refuses without changing files.

tests.covers: A drifted context line makes the installer raise with bytes untouched; a second apply of each patch is refused; a wrong pin fails snapshot verification.

cases.use: pi or OpenCode crashes or exits during a turn; the turn is reported as failed and the Agent can be restarted.

tests.covers: Real host and bridge with simulated pi and OpenCode that exit mid-turn: the turn fails with its partial answer and an exit notice, the bridge ends so the host reports the Agent stopped and refuses new prompts, and a restarted Agent completes a turn.

cases.use: The saved harness is not installed when Agent starts; the start fails with a clear message instead of hanging or silently running something else.

tests.covers: Real host launch preparation with pi and then OpenCode selected but not installed: the start fails with the install-it-in-Settings message, the launch task is failed and nothing is started in its place.

cases.use: The user enables Plan, GSA or RSA while pi or OpenCode is the harness, a combination the documentation calls not qualified; it either works or is refused explicitly.

tests.covers: Real host with simulated pi as the Agent runtime: a multi-line Plan contract reaches pi intact and its question form returns in the transcript; GSA and RSA starts are refused with an explicit message and prepare no run, and are admitted again without a harness runtime.

cases.use: After stopping a harness turn the next request works.

tests.covers: After cancelAll the next request is served and pi returns to waiting after an abort.

cases.use: When the app stops, no harness or model process started for the session survives.

tests.covers: Four seconds after the host stops, no process references the run workspace.

cases.use: The installed harness was built from another patch set, pin or entry point; it is recognised as not current and the bridge is refreshed.

tests.covers: The receipt check is false for an empty patch list, changed entry-point bytes or another pin; refresh-bridge replaces an older bridge and a second run reports reuse.

cases.use: Harness patches can be reversed to the exact original files, leaving unrelated files alone.

tests.covers: Reverse apply in reverse order restores the original bytes and keeps an unrelated file.

areas.label: Task Graph: checked execution around the Agent

cases.use: A request to inspect, edit or test the workspace is run inside a checked graph; a plain question takes the direct path.

tests.covers: Production auto-route classifies eight Italian and English prompts as direct, read-only or workspace-write and builds a three-node graph that requires a tool result and a receipt check (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: With a real model, a workspace task completes inside its graph and the graph journal ends as succeeded.

tests.covers: A workspace-write request on real weights takes the automatic Task Graph route; the graph read back from its journal must end succeeded and total.txt must hold the independently computed total. Not yet run.

cases.use: A graph is validated, created, started and runs to success with its events in order.

tests.covers: Real host API: validate, create, start, poll to succeeded with two completed nodes and contiguous event sequence numbers, and the graph listed.
A diamond graph moves through ready and running with left and right in parallel and the join and graph succeed (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: A graph or a node that requires approval waits until the user approves it.

tests.covers: An approval-required graph is created as validated and becomes ready on approve; an approval node waits and its approve call is accepted.
Start is refused before approval; after approval the graph and an approval node succeed (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: A graph action writes a file and a gate verifies it, or runs a test command and checks its result.

tests.covers: The native write changes the file, the assert gate passes, and a test.run node spawns a real python3 command whose gate passes (make test-task-graph-unit).
A native write-plus-assert graph over HTTP succeeds and the written file has the expected content.

cases.use: The user pauses a running graph and resumes it.

tests.covers: Pause during a slow node stays paused after a tick and resume completes (make test-task-graph-unit).
Pause during a 120 ms node reaches paused and resume is accepted; completion after resume is not asserted.

cases.use: The user cancels a running graph; the graph and its running node end as cancelled.

tests.covers: Cancelling a running graph cancels graph and node (make test-task-graph-unit).
Cancel during a five-second node ends graph and node as cancelled.

cases.use: The user opens the Task Graph dialog from the IDE.

tests.covers: The IDE Task Graph button opens the dialog (with an empty mocked list) and Back returns to the transcript.

cases.use: The user watches a running graph's nodes change state in the dialog and pauses or resumes it there.

tests.covers: Production dialog against the real host scheduler and journal (synthetic executor): Start runs the graph, node cards follow the host states, Pause holds the remaining nodes, Resume runs them to success and the durable events are listed.

cases.use: An optional node fails; dependants that run on any terminal outcome still run and the graph succeeds.

tests.covers: An optional failed node with a terminal-condition dependent ends with cleanup and graph succeeded (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: A node without a configured timeout may run for hours; an explicit timeout is honoured and preserved.

tests.covers: timeoutMs 0 and 1234 are accepted and round-trip while invalid values are rejected; an untimed node still runs after four simulated hours and a 1,000 ms one is cancelled (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: Two graphs want the model or the same workspace; only one model turn and one writer run at a time.

tests.covers: Of two graphs with agent turns only one runs until the first is cancelled; a second workspace-write graph stays ready while the first runs (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: Validation, scheduling and journal replay stay fast and deterministic for many graphs and longer chains.

tests.covers: 1,000 parse-and-validate rounds and six runs of an eight-node chain with identical replayed sequence numbers finish inside their bounds (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: Only allowed state transitions, identifiers and relative paths are accepted.

tests.covers: Identifier and relative-path validators and the allowed and forbidden node and graph transitions (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: An oversized graph definition or request body is refused with a bounded error.

tests.covers: Real host API: 257 nodes, a 4097-byte goal, a 16385-byte action text, more than 65536 JSON tokens and a body one byte over 2 MiB are refused with a short error naming the limit; nothing is persisted and status stays responsive.

cases.use: A malformed JSON body or an invalid graph (cycle, duplicate id, escaping path, missing dependency) is rejected with an explanation.

tests.covers: Nine malformed bodies and eight invalid graphs are rejected with error text (make test-task-graph-unit).
A self-dependency graph gets 422 from the validate endpoint.

cases.use: The model says it is done without a tool result, or the marker comes before the result; the action is not marked successful.

tests.covers: The completion contract accepts a marker after the tool result and rejects a marker before a late result and prose with no tool call (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: A node asks for a capability its policy does not grant; the graph is rejected.

tests.covers: A read-only node declaring a workspace write is rejected by policy (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: A graph names an executor that is not available; start is refused and nothing changes.

tests.covers: A proposal without an executor validates as not executable and start answers 422 with state, revision and sequence unchanged.
Start is refused "not registered" with state and event sequence unchanged (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: A request carries an outdated sequence number or lacks the app's request header; it is refused.

tests.covers: Create without the request header gets 403 and start with a stale expected sequence gets 409.

cases.use: A node keeps failing; after its allowed attempts the graph fails.

tests.covers: A failing node with two allowed attempts fails the graph after exactly two (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: The Agent turn of a graph ends with a runtime error; the node, the graph and the durable result are failed and stay failed after reload.

tests.covers: A graph agent turn ending with a turn error is failed in task, node, graph and receipt, and a reload agrees; the same turn ending normally succeeds (make test-remote-turn-error).

cases.use: The graph is locked by another process or its journal holds an invalid line; the operation is refused rather than guessing.

tests.covers: With the graph lock held start is refused "locked"; a journal line with a duplicate key makes the load fail with a named error (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: The user asks to undo a step that ran a command; no automatic undo is offered or claimed.

tests.covers: Undo of a test.run node reports "No automatic undo" and is not applied (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: The user undoes a step whose exact file write was recorded; the previous bytes are restored.

tests.covers: Undo restores the previous file content and reports fully reversed (make test-task-graph-unit).
The node undo endpoint removes the written file and reports applied and fully reversed.

cases.use: The app crashes between writing the journal and the state file, or leaves a torn line; on reload the graph state is rebuilt from the journal and continues.

tests.covers: A torn journal line is ignored on reload; failpoints after the event append and before the state rename leave a graph that reloads as running and completes (make test-task-graph-unit).

cases.use: The user restarts the app and reopens a paused or finished graph from the dialog.

tests.covers: The host process is stopped and started again and a new app window opens: the dialog lists the paused and the finished graph from their journals without new events, and the paused one resumes and finishes without rerunning its completed step.

areas.label: Open Blueprint: code maps with verified citations

cases.use: In Agent the user opens Blueprint, picks a diagram kind and focus and asks for a map; the Agent is prompted to write the blueprint file.

tests.covers: Production page on the real workspace handlers with a scripted agent stream: Map it sends the production prompt with the file path, schema and evidence contract and the folder is created by the real mkdir endpoint.
The production prompt builder names the focus, one write call to the path, the schema and the evidence contract.

cases.use: A real model maps a repository; components, relationships and citations match the code.

tests.covers: Real DeepSeek weights: the Agent writes an architecture map and a cache-miss sequence of a held-out fixture; the production validator and verifier grade components, relationships, step order and the share of quotes found in the cited files.

cases.use: The diagram appears and grows while the Agent is still writing the blueprint file.

tests.covers: Streamed body deltas draw one node, then four, then edges with a live banner and no evidence badge until the file is on disk.
Every prefix of the spec text parses without throwing and never loses nodes.

cases.use: The user clicks a node and sees its citations with their verification state and its neighbours.

tests.covers: A node shows "Partly verified" with verified and moved citations and its neighbours lit.

cases.use: The user traces what a node reaches and finds a route between two nodes, including when none exists.

tests.covers: Upstream reach is shown, a route reports two steps with its hops and another pair reports "No route".
Reach up and down including a cycle, an existing route, no route and a null self route.

cases.use: The user hides a group with a lens chip and finds a node by text.

tests.covers: The Data lens hides and restores a node and its edge; Find plus Enter opens the matching node and the spec file is unchanged.

cases.use: The user opens a citation in the IDE at the quoted lines and returns to the blueprint.

tests.covers: A citation opens the IDE with the quoted line selected through the real read handler and Back returns to the blueprint.

cases.use: The user exports the blueprint as a standalone HTML page that works offline.

tests.covers: The exported file has no external resources and, opened from disk, shows the nodes, the verified-claims count and node highlighting.

cases.use: The user exports the blueprint as SVG or JSON.

tests.covers: The SVG opened from disk shows the four parts, their verification marks and its own styles with no script or external reference; the JSON reopens with 5 of 8 verified, and a blueprint shown as its group overview still exports all twelve parts.

cases.use: The user opens a sequence blueprint and sees lifelines with numbered steps.

tests.covers: A sequence file shows three lifelines, steps numbered one to five and a route between participants.
A participant named only by steps is added with an issue and steps keep order and call or return types.

cases.use: The user maps and opens the Workflow, Data flow or Lifecycle diagram kinds.

tests.covers: Each kind is chosen on the New card and mapped: the production prompt names the kind and its node types, and the written file is drawn with those node types, the kind's default relationship type and its verified-claims count.
Prompt, node-type fallback, default relationship type and layout direction of Workflow, Data flow and Lifecycle.

cases.use: The user presses Implement code; the Agent is asked, in the same conversation, to build what the blueprint describes.

tests.covers: Implement code sends the implement prompt with the path in the same conversation with no engine restart or new session.
The implement prompt for code and description bases, with steps numbered without gaps.

cases.use: The user sends the blueprint to Design; Design starts in a design folder and the blueprint goes with the first brief.

tests.covers: Send to Design starts Design on the design folder, shows the hand-off card, sends nothing before the brief and then sends parts, relationships and brief once.
The Design brief lists parts by group and relationships.

cases.use: A blueprint with more items than allowed is capped with each drop reported, and a long chain opens readable with Fit.

tests.covers: Forty-five nodes are capped at forty with issues reported and a 60-node, 200-edge hand-off stays under 26,000 characters.
A 14-node chain opens at a readable zoom with the first node in view and Fit shows the whole drawing.

cases.use: The code has circular relationships; the diagram lays them out and tracing terminates.

tests.covers: Layout marks a cycle edge as back and reach across a cycle terminates.

cases.use: Many citations point at the same or very large files; each file is read once and reading is bounded.

tests.covers: Verification reads each cited file once and with a file bound of one reports skipped items.

cases.use: The same blueprint always lays out the same way with no overlapping nodes.

tests.covers: Layout is deterministic with no overlapping boxes and every node inside its lane.

cases.use: The user opens the new-blueprint card over an existing drawing and dismisses it; the drawing is untouched.

tests.covers: The New card focuses its field, closes with Escape and the close button, and the four nodes remain.

cases.use: The blueprint file is not valid JSON or uses another schema; the user is told it cannot be drawn.

tests.covers: A truncated file shows "This blueprint cannot be drawn" and "Not valid JSON" with no nodes.
A foreign schema is an error.

cases.use: A cited quote is not at the cited lines, the file is missing or no quote is given; the claim is marked moved, unverified or unsourced.

tests.covers: Against the workspace bytes the header shows 5 of 8 claims verified with verified, partial, unverified and unsourced items.
The verifier returns verified, moved, unverified, missing and unquoted for the corresponding sources.

cases.use: The blueprint names unknown endpoints, duplicate items or paths outside the project; they are dropped and reported.

tests.covers: Duplicate and id-less nodes, unknown types, ../ and absolute paths, unknown endpoints and duplicate edges are dropped with a report each.

cases.use: Names or descriptions contain HTML or script; the diagram shows them as text.

tests.covers: The SVG renderer emits only drawing tags, no event attributes and escapes labels as text.

cases.use: The Agent ends its turn without writing a usable blueprint file; the panel reports that instead of showing an empty map.

tests.covers: A map turn that ends without writing its file reports "ended its turn without saving" the path, with no pending map and no blank form; a written file with no nodes reports "the diagram has no nodes"; nothing is drawn.

cases.use: The user presses Send to Design while the Agent is still working; the engine switch must be confirmed first.

tests.covers: With the Agent still working, Send to Design asks "Interrupt the current generation?"; Cancel starts and interrupts nothing and keeps the Agent conversation, Switch anyway starts Design on design/.

cases.use: After a reload the last blueprint opens again with its verification state.

tests.covers: After reload the last blueprint reopens with 5 of 8 verified and Back returns to the composer.

cases.use: The blueprint file changes on disk; Refresh redraws it.

tests.covers: After the file is replaced by a 14-node chain, Refresh redraws it.

cases.use: The cited code changes after the map was made; the user re-checks and outdated citations are flagged.

tests.covers: After the cited code is edited, Refresh re-reads the files: 4 of 8 verified, the rewritten call not found, the shifted quotes flagged at their new lines and the blueprint file unchanged; restoring the code restores 5 of 8.

areas.label: LAN access, remote endpoints, cloud API and the /v1 endpoint

cases.use: The user enables LAN access; the host reports its LAN address and serves the UI there, and disabling turns it off again.

tests.covers: Real host /api/lan enable returns the LAN address and port; from that address lan-health and the page answer (skipped when the machine has no LAN IPv4); disable reports lan false.

cases.use: From another device on the LAN the user opens the UI over plain http and chats, copies and regenerates.

tests.covers: The production page on a non-loopback http origin without secure-context APIs: a prompt streams and completes, Copy succeeds through the fallback and Regenerate works.

cases.use: On the device the user enters the host address; it is normalised and probed before use.

tests.covers: Production functions add the default port, keep an explicit one, strip path and query, resolve the current host and request the host's lan-health endpoint.

cases.use: The host shares its running Cowork folder; a device pairs with the code, sends prompts and reads the answers.

tests.covers: Production UI on both sides with the real host and Cowork runtime and a simulated model: Settings shows an eight-digit code, the device pairs, sends a prompt and reads the reply, and the host lists one paired device.
Real host and Cowork runtime with requests from the LAN address: sharing returns a pairing code, pairing returns a token, and the paired device's send and poll return the simulated reply.

cases.use: A LAN device publishes its conversations so the host can list them.

tests.covers: A device snapshot with chat, agent and design conversations is stored and listed by the host, also when posted from the LAN address.
In LAN mode the production store saves a 6 MiB chat in the browser with no request to the host-private history endpoint and restores it on reload.

cases.use: Another program calls DStudio's OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint and gets the engine's exact response.

tests.covers: Real host relay with a stand-in engine: GET /v1/models and POST chat completions are forwarded with exact method, path and body and the response returned byte for byte.
Checked prompts are answered by a real Qwen model through the host /v1 proxy.

cases.use: The user points Agent or Design at a remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the model runs remotely while the tools run locally.
