tests.covers: A second DStudio host serves the real default model; the client host runs Agent and Design against it and each writes its marker file in its own workspace with the local write tool.
The built Agent in remote structured mode receives tool schemas and executes authored tool calls locally.
A 100,000-repetition Unicode request passes from the runtime through the host worker to a loopback peer intact (cases in model_rpc_input_test.c).

The real client host and built Agent, through a second host's /v1 proxy, against a scripted ds4-server that sends the DSML write as text and again as tool_calls: the file is written once, a plain turn completes and the automatic correctness graph succeeds without retrying the turn.
A request without tool schemas (DSML runtime): the relay delivers ds4-server's DSML text and finish reason, publishes none of its tool_calls copy, and refuses tool calls that arrive without any text.

cases.use: The user configures the DeepSeek API as the backend and runs the Agent with it.

tests.covers: A running launcher starts the Agent with the remote backend on the billed DeepSeek API and completes GSA phases; no local weights are involved.

cases.use: A remote endpoint is reached over HTTPS with certificate verification.

tests.covers: The whole stream corpus is repeated through the host worker over TLS with an isolated certificate authority and verification on.

cases.use: The user enters the remote base URL, model name and API key; they are used for the next request.

tests.covers: The host parses an http or https remote URL and model without touching globals (make test-lan-unit).
A request admitted before a key change carries the old key and the next one the new key (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).

cases.use: The user enters and saves a cloud API key or a remote endpoint in the Settings Connection pane and switches the backend there.

tests.covers: Enters a Server URL and then a DeepSeek key in Settings -> Connection, switches the backend and the cloud model: each chat goes to the chosen endpoint with the saved key, and a reopened page keeps the settings (simulated provider and endpoint).

cases.use: A client of the /v1 endpoint asks for a tool call; the model returns it with exact arguments and uses the tool result in its next answer.

tests.covers: Through the host /v1 proxy a real Qwen model returns one forced read_stock call with exact arguments and answers with the supplied tool result.
The same forced tool call and follow-up on the native endpoint of ds4-server with DeepSeek and Laguna weights.

cases.use: A pairing code works once and is voided after five wrong attempts.

tests.covers: Five wrong codes void the code so the right one fails; a new code pairs once and a second use fails; the stored device file holds no token and is private.

cases.use: A LAN device can reach the page, health, the /v1 endpoint and web tools, and nothing host-private.

tests.covers: The route table: loopback bind allows only the page, remote chat, mirror and health; LAN bind adds /v1 and web tools; start, files, PDF, design, store and LAN control never (make test-lan-unit).
From the LAN address the web-tool preflights answer with CORS and host-only routes answer 403 (skipped when the machine has no LAN IPv4).

cases.use: Browser pages from loopback and private addresses may call the API; pages from foreign origins get no permission.

tests.covers: Preflights from eight loopback, private or allowed origins get the allow header and seven foreign ones do not.
The relay adds CORS headers for a LAN caller with an accepted origin and none without (make test-v1-relay).

cases.use: Only private, usable IPv4 addresses are offered for LAN access.

tests.covers: Loopback and link-local are rejected, the private ranges accepted and 172.32 treated as not private (make test-lan-unit).

cases.use: A paired device uploads a file naming another folder; it still lands in the shared folder.

tests.covers: An attach-file request naming another directory writes into the shared folder and leaves the other one empty.

cases.use: Very large bodies and very long request paths pass through the /v1 endpoint intact, and only minimal headers reach the engine.

tests.covers: A 1,023-byte path and a 90 kB fragmented body are forwarded intact and client Authorization headers are not passed on.

cases.use: The host keeps device histories for a bounded number of devices and total size, dropping the oldest.

tests.covers: The mirror keeps at most 32 devices and about 256 MiB, evicting the least recently published.

cases.use: On a plain-http LAN origin the browser lacks secure-context APIs; the UI still works.

tests.covers: With isSecureContext false and no randomUUID or clipboard API the page loads without errors and stays on its origin.
A LAN-client profile on the startup page goes straight to the app without posting an engine start.

cases.use: With a cloud backend or as a LAN client, local-only features (native vision, forced SSD streaming, on-disk session commands) are not offered.

tests.covers: Cloud backend and LAN-client mode get no local native-vision capability.
Session save, list, switch and delete are hidden for active LAN Cowork.
Forced SSD streaming is not effective for a remote model (make test-engine-setup-unit).

cases.use: A remote request body above 16 MiB is refused before any network call.

tests.covers: A body one byte over 16 MiB launches no worker and returns an error naming the limit (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).
Decoded bodies of 16 MiB and 24 MiB are refused with an error naming 16 MiB (cases in model_rpc_input_test.c).

cases.use: A browser reaches the host under a foreign host name (DNS rebinding); the request is refused.

tests.covers: An unknown Host header gets 421 on status and store requests while loopback, the LAN IP, .local and allowed names work.

cases.use: A LAN device calls a host-only route (start, status, history, files, wipe); it gets 403.

tests.covers: A LAN-origin GET of the history store gets 403.
A paired device's token gets 403 on store, start, status, sharing control, design files and wipe.
With the host bound to all interfaces the workspace file routes are not LAN-public (make test-agent-workspace).

cases.use: A device enters a wrong code or uses no or an unknown token; it gets nothing.

tests.covers: A wrong code on the device shows "Wrong code".
A device with no token or an unknown one gets 403 on status, send and poll; sharing cannot be enabled before Cowork runs or by a device.

cases.use: A paired device sends slash commands, control frames or a goal; only plain prompts are accepted.

tests.covers: Device prompts /list and /del, a control frame and a goal orchestration get 403 host_only.

cases.use: A state-changing request lacks the app's request header or carries an invalid device id; it is refused.

tests.covers: POST to store and LAN control without the request header get 403 and a mirror snapshot with a bad client id gets 400.
A text/plain mirror post without the header gets 403 and nothing is stored.

cases.use: The address entered on the device does not answer or is another application; the user is told.

tests.covers: The probe rejects "Cannot reach" when the fetch throws and "not a DStudio LAN host" for another app.

cases.use: The remote endpoint returns an error event, malformed JSON, several choices or an incomplete stream; the turn fails with an error instead of a fabricated answer.

tests.covers: Provider error events, duplicate JSON keys, wrong or multiple choices and missing completions end in a model error with no batch.
Invalid escapes, lone surrogates, embedded NUL and truncated envelopes yield a model error and no network request (cases in model_rpc_input_test.c).

cases.use: The remote endpoint cannot be reached; the turn fails with a connection error.

tests.covers: An endpoint on a closed port produces a model error mentioning the connection (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).

cases.use: A remote backend is requested in a mode or with options it cannot have; the start is refused.

tests.covers: A remote start outside Agent or Design and a LAN client without a host are refused (make test-lan-unit).
Remote Agent, Cowork and Design starts with SSD streaming on are refused with unsupported_memory_mode (make test-launch-preflight).
An unknown remote tool protocol makes the runtime exit with "unsupported remote tool protocol" and no request.

cases.use: The cloud API key is missing, wrong or out of credit; the error from the provider is shown and nothing is retried silently.

tests.covers: A wrong (401) and an out-of-credit (402) key show the provider's own error once with Retry and no further request; an emptied key is refused with a message and nothing is sent to the provider or to the local model.

cases.use: A message contains invalid bytes; they are replaced visibly instead of corrupting the request.

tests.covers: Thirteen invalid wire strings are rejected and invalid input bytes become replacement characters in the messages snapshot (make test-remote-utf8).

cases.use: The host revokes a paired device; its token stops working immediately.

tests.covers: Revoke empties the device list and the device's token then gets 403.
After revoke the device list is empty and the device's status request gets 403.

cases.use: The host stops sharing or restarts Cowork in another folder; the device is told the folder is no longer shared.

tests.covers: After sharing is disabled or Cowork restarts elsewhere the device gets not_shared.

cases.use: The host restarts; paired devices are remembered but sharing is off until enabled again.

tests.covers: After a restart on the same data folder sharing is disabled, the paired device persists and its token sees sharing false.

cases.use: A runtime using a remote model restarts; the saved conversation is restored and resent exactly.

tests.covers: After a kill the restored session resends the previous conversation unchanged and an old tool-call id is not run again.

cases.use: A reply from a previous remote request arrives after its connection was replaced; it leaks nothing into the new one.

tests.covers: After the runtime pipe is closed and its descriptor number reused, the old response leaks zero bytes and the old worker is reaped (cases in model_rpc_lifecycle_test.c).

cases.use: The user switches to a cloud provider while a local request is being prepared; the local request is dropped and not sent to the wrong backend.

tests.covers: A local request waiting on an auxiliary stop while the user selects a cloud provider is rejected and no model request follows.

cases.use: After working with a cloud backend the user switches back to the local model.

tests.covers: After cloud turns, selecting Local in Connection starts the saved local GGUF (not the cloud model) through /api/start, sends the next turn to the local engine without the key and continues the same conversation.

areas.label: First launch, engine installation, upgrade and recovery

cases.use: On a new computer with no network the user launches the app, presses Install and the engine is built from the bundled sources and discovered.

tests.covers: The signed app is relocated and started with an empty profile and outbound network denied; headless WebKit clicks Install: the engine is built from bundled sources at the pinned commit and its tools run. No weights or inference.

cases.use: During onboarding the user also sets up Laguna and llama.cpp; they build offline and share the model store.

tests.covers: Choosing the Laguna model builds Laguna from bundled sources with its store linked to the main one; the app's install-engine command builds llama.cpp offline with a bundled-source receipt.

cases.use: The engines are installed with the app's install-engine command into an empty folder and their tools start.

tests.covers: The built host binary installs main, Laguna and llama.cpp into a new root; each receipt is readable and the built tools answer --help or --version. Network is not denied in this run.

cases.use: Installing an engine copies the bundled sources byte for byte, with file modes and a provenance receipt.

tests.covers: The production installer copies exact bytes and modes, writes the source receipt and leaves no staging folder; the three shipped snapshots copy and verify.

cases.use: The app reports which engine revisions it ships, from any install location.

tests.covers: The built binary's engine-pins command lists main, Laguna and llama.cpp with commits matching the manifest, writes nothing and gives the same answer from a relocated path with spaces.

cases.use: llama.cpp and the MLX runtime are installed with outbound network denied.

tests.covers: A real offline build of the dynamic llama.cpp layout under a network-denying sandbox: receipt lists server and libraries, load commands stay inside the tree and a copied tree runs.
A real MLX installation into a new root with network denied: pinned versions in the receipt and the installed server command starts with offline mode set.

cases.use: The Agent, Cowork, Design and Chat lookup runtimes are built from the engine sources with DStudio's patches, leaving the checkout untouched.

tests.covers: Source-only copies of main and Laguna are really compiled and linked into Agent, Cowork, Design and the Chat lookup server; originals stay hash-identical and the built runtimes run their tool and interrupt tests with authored model frames.
Production builder with a stand-in compiler: sources untouched, both runtimes published with the manifest stamp and an unchanged repeat invokes no compiler.
A real Design build from a Git-less source archive: the runtime starts, its stamp is the archive form and status is up to date.

cases.use: The user checks for engine updates; the check reports status without fetching or changing sources.

tests.covers: Real host update check answers with no action for the engine section and never invokes Git.

cases.use: The app serves its startup page and main page from the installed bundle.

tests.covers: The loading page and the main page, including first-launch URLs, are served identical to the shipped files.
The page readers return the main page, loading page and annotator script from disk (make test-lan-unit).

cases.use: The desktop window shows the web UI under the native title bar: the window buttons work, the top strip drags the window and the content below stays usable.

tests.covers: A real Cocoa window and web view made by the production wrapper with a fixture page: full-size content, the 28 px inset, a drag strip that also works after a resize and hit-testable window buttons (make test-macos-window-theme).

cases.use: The user double-clicks the app in Finder for the first time; the window opens on the startup or onboarding screen.
cases.uncoveredReason: Needs the native desktop session and Finder (P7 desktop matrix); not exercisable by a headless test.

cases.use: The app or engine folder lives in a path with spaces or was moved; installation, builds and shaders still work.

tests.covers: A probe linked to the built Metal objects initialises the shader library from the engine folder and from an unrelated workspace with spaces, checking 257 GPU additions against a scalar result.
The Chat lookup builder runs on a checkout in a folder with spaces.

cases.use: An unchanged engine is not rebuilt; a changed source, header, compiler flag or shader triggers exactly one rebuild.

tests.covers: Production Design builder with a stand-in compiler: repeat build compiles nothing; changed support header, flags, an untracked GPU header and a changed compiler wrapper each rebuild once.
An unchanged rebuild is cached and a newer Metal source forces one relink.
A newer Metal source, even in the same second, invalidates the server binary (make test-lan-unit).

cases.use: Two installations or builds are started together; independent ones overlap safely and conflicting ones are refused as busy.

tests.covers: Two installs to different targets overlap at a barrier and both complete; a held source lease makes a second install fail.
While a Design build is held, Design, Agent and Chat builds each exit "build is busy".
The exclusive install lock is refused while a shared server lease is held and the reverse.
With one installer parked mid-build a second is refused at once and stages nothing; the leader publishes once; installations in two roots overlap.
Real host: a second download request is refused (409) and a second installer exits busy while the first holds the lease.

cases.use: The installer chooses the build recipe for the platform and the toolchains actually present.

tests.covers: Production recipes with simulated toolchains: macOS static, Linux and Windows dynamic with CPU variants and a module per detected backend.
Requirements for Python 3.12 to 3.14 pin every package with the matching-ABI hash, and interpreter discovery prefers a supported one.
Real make with stand-in compilers: Agent, Chat lookup and Design link lines match upstream for Metal, CPU, CUDA and ROCm.

cases.use: An engine already listening on the engine port (another DStudio or a user process) is not stopped by installation or shutdown.

tests.covers: The process listening on the engine port (an existing engine or a test-owned sentinel) is unchanged after every step and at shutdown.
On termination the host leaves an external server alive and stops only the child it owns (make test-engine-setup-unit).
An upgrade attempt while the earlier server runs is refused and the server keeps running; it proceeds once the model stops.
The same for a running MLX server.

cases.use: A second DStudio instance sees that the engine is owned by the first and does not take it over.

tests.covers: The instance-lock function returns the owner pid while the lock file is held and 0 after unlock (make test-lan-unit).

cases.use: On a profile that has not finished onboarding, the startup screen opens the app without trying to start an engine.

tests.covers: A not-onboarded profile and an empty profile both go to the app with no engine start and no POST.

cases.use: Bundled source manifests with escaping paths, too many files or too many bytes are refused.

tests.covers: Manifest paths that escape or name stores are rejected as inventory errors and file, byte and manifest limits are enforced.

cases.use: A bundled source file is missing, extra, altered or replaced by a link; installation fails and nothing is fetched from the network.

tests.covers: Missing, extra and tampered files, linked or special files and a linked manifest are rejected with the target never created.
Changed wheel bytes, an extra wheel and a wheel replaced by a link are rejected by wheel verification.
A truncated, altered, missing or extra file in the bundled llama.cpp snapshot fails the upgrade with nothing published and no stage kept; network denied.
An altered, truncated, missing or extra bundled wheel fails the upgrade before any stage; the earlier runtime is byte-identical.

cases.use: The selected engine folder carries a receipt for an engine DStudio does not run; it is refused and left untouched.

tests.covers: Real host startup with a persisted checkout whose receipt names another engine or none: no repair is attempted, choosing it answers 400 unsupported_engine and its files are unchanged.
A checkout whose receipt names another engine is unsupported and server, agent, cowork and design spawns refuse with no child (make test-engine-setup-unit).
Starts against a checkout with an unsupported or missing engine receipt are refused with engine_model_mismatch (make test-launch-preflight).

cases.use: An old client or script asks to set up a retired engine; the request is refused and nothing is installed.

tests.covers: A direct request to the retired Qwen setup route gets 404 and nothing is installed.
A retired engine id is rejected by copy and install with nothing created.
A stale request to run the "latest engine" update answers 409 without invoking Git or changing engine files.

cases.use: The folder chosen for the engine already holds other data; installation refuses and preserves it.

tests.covers: A target holding user data, also through a symlink alias, is refused with data and inode preserved; a target that gains a file during copy is rejected.
Installing into a root whose engine folder holds user data refuses and leaves the bytes intact (make test-engine-setup-unit).

cases.use: Compiling or linking a runtime fails or produces an unusable binary; the previous working runtime and the sources are kept.

tests.covers: A link failure or a missing output exits 1 with both old runtimes and the sources preserved and no stamp.
A failing linker and empty, non-executable or linked outputs keep the old executable, stamp and every source byte.
A failed make with partial output keeps the previous working binary and no version stamp; invalid linker outputs are refused.
Configure failure, build failure with a half-linked server, no server produced, or a server reporting another build keep the earlier runtime and only the build log (at most two).

cases.use: The engine sources drifted, are partly patched or were edited during the build; the patch or build is refused and no file is changed.

tests.covers: Production patcher: already applied, partly applied, changed context, ambiguous and malformed patches are rejected with the output untouched (make test-unified-patch).
The production patch script on a copy of the bundled sources: a previously shipped port, a user-modified shader and a partial state are each refused without touching files.
The production Agent patcher rejects an already patched source, a one-byte drift and a partial hunk with the copy unchanged.
A contributor-edited header makes the patch partial and a header edited during compilation is detected: nothing is published and the edit is kept.
Production Agent patcher on copies of the installed sources: a second apply and a drifted anchor are rejected with the file unchanged and an unrelated comment survives (make test-steering-patch).
A drifted mlx-lm patch fails real git apply --check; the earlier runtime stays selected and usable.
The host refuses a main checkout at the earlier pin as drift before any build; models, settings and the built server are byte-identical.

cases.use: A lock file, staging folder, source or output in the install path is a symlink or was swapped; the operation refuses and nothing outside is touched.

tests.covers: A symlinked build lock is refused with its target unchanged.
A staging folder swapped for a symlink during the build is refused and the foreign folder preserved.
A stage replaced by a symlink or another folder no longer matches and cleanup follows only the owned descriptor (make test-unified-patch).
A foreign or dangling link in place of the shared model store is refused and preserved (make test-engine-setup-unit).

cases.use: A required compiler backend or Python interpreter is missing; the installer says so instead of producing a broken install.

tests.covers: A requested backend without its toolchain, an unknown backend and Metal off macOS raise.
With no supported interpreter the finder raises "needs Python".
No CMake anywhere fails before staging with the earlier runtime kept; the host CLI names a missing python3.
No supported Python and no git fail with the earlier runtime kept; only a log is retained when a command ran.

cases.use: An installed engine has changed, extra or linked files; it is not treated as a current installation.

tests.covers: An unrecorded module, changed bytes, a deleted module or a module replaced by a link make the receipt check fail.
One byte appended to the installed interpreter makes the receipt check fail.
Bytes appended to the built Design binary make status report "needs rebuild".
A tampered server, a receipt with a missing binary or another pin is rebuilt; a receipt naming another engine or format, a truncated receipt or a linked directory is preserved and refused.
A tampered or missing interpreter, a changed base Python or another wheel set is rebuilt; another engine, format, truncated receipt or link is preserved and refused.

cases.use: The engine folder lacks its Agent source or holds an old in-place modification; startup reports the exact problem and preserves the files.

tests.covers: A Laguna checkout without its Agent source reports the missing file and a legacy-patched one reports "already modified" with source and backup preserved.
Restore with a legacy marker and an unverified backup exits 1 with source and backup unchanged.

cases.use: The disk fills up while an engine is being copied or built; the failure is reported and a later retry works.

tests.covers: The production main source installer and the host's --install-engine llama hit a real ENOSPC on task-owned HFS+ volumes while copying and while building (stand-in cmake): the cause is reported, nothing is published, no partial copy or objects keep the space, and a retry installs.

cases.use: DStudio's engine adaptations can be applied, applied again harmlessly and restored to the exact original files, preserving unrelated edits.

tests.covers: On a private copy of a managed checkout the eight native adaptations are reversed newest first and reapplied to byte-identical files with an unrelated note unchanged.
The same round trip on the sources just installed by the app restores them byte for byte.
The metrics patch script on isolated copies: apply, repeat apply, restore twice to exact bytes, unrelated comment preserved, partial and drifted sources refused.
The pairing patch script: applicable, applied, already applied, restored byte-exact and already restored.

The Laguna prefill batch patch on copies of the bundled engine: apply, repeat, byte-exact restore, drift and partial patches refused, local edits kept, main skipped, CPU build and the engine resolver.
The prepare patch script across two files with unrelated edits: apply, repeat, restore and second restore; partial state and symlinks refused.

cases.use: An engine folder patched by an older DStudio version is brought to the current patch level, or refused cleanly if it cannot be.

tests.covers: Reconstructed with Git on scratch copies: each recorded older delta reverses to its previous hash and reapplies exactly, and the patcher output equals the recorded derived source.
Web and server patch bases: the native transformer equals the recorded derived bytes and Git apply, repeat and reverse agree.
The previously shipped port is refused as drift rather than migrated.
An older MLX receipt (no base interpreter, another manifest or patch set) is not current, and the three patches apply, refuse a repeat and reverse exactly.
An installation with the earlier patch set and mlx-lm wheel is replaced atomically by the current set; the guard starts the new interpreter and refuses the old identity.
The b11371 installation is replaced by the bundled pin; settings, projects, sessions, models and KV bytes are identical and the guard refuses the old binary identity.

cases.use: The user installs a new DStudio version over an existing profile with engines, models, settings and history; everything is found and brought up to date.
cases.uncoveredReason: DStudio has no in-place upgrade of an earlier main ds4 engine checkout (refused as source drift; PLAN.MD P5); llama.cpp/MLX upgrades and data preservation are covered separately by test-install-recovery.

cases.use: Running the installer again on a current installation reuses it without rebuilding.

tests.covers: A second install call returns reused and not built.
A second installation reports reused.
A repeat build of the real runtimes exits 0.
A current installation is verified and reused without a second publication, also beside a running server.

cases.use: An installation is interrupted before or just after publication; the next attempt neither loses data nor piles up leftovers.

tests.covers: A failed folder sync after publication is reported as published with bytes and receipt present; two failed preparations are retained and a third attempt is refused.

Stand-in cmake: the installer killed (SIGKILL) or canceled (group SIGTERM) at six barriers from source copy to after publication leaves the earlier runtime or the complete new one, frees the lease, and the next run completes; three killed builds do not block a fourth.
Stand-in CPython: the same six points including wheel verification; a stage left by a killed installer is removed by the next one and an installation moved aside is put back.
Real main/Laguna snapshots: a source installer killed mid-copy or terminated before publication publishes nothing; the next run completes and keeps one retained candidate.

cases.use: A build is killed (the builder or its whole process group); nothing half-built is published and the next build succeeds.

tests.covers: With the build group killed, sources and runtimes are intact and a new build succeeds; with only the parent killed competing builds are refused until the compiler ends.
Parent-only and whole-group kills publish nothing and a retry succeeds.
Real offline CMake build over an earlier installation, killed with its process group after 25 objects: the earlier runtime stays; the next run removes the stage and publishes the pinned server.

cases.use: After the engine sources change the runtime is reported as needing a rebuild and rebuilding gives a new stamp.

tests.covers: Appending to a source file gives "needs rebuild" and the rebuild produces a different stamp with status up to date.

cases.use: Leftover staging folders from earlier builds are cleaned up within bounds without touching unrelated files.

tests.covers: An intact stage is removed, cleanup of a 160-file stage is visit-bounded and unrelated files survive (make test-unified-patch).

cases.use: An optional engine's empty model folder is replaced by a link to the shared store, and doing it again changes nothing.

tests.covers: An empty optional model folder is replaced by the link and a repeat keeps the same inode (make test-engine-setup-unit).

cases.use: After installing, the user reloads the page; installed engines are listed and the app still verifies as signed.

tests.covers: After a browser reload both checkouts are listed with their servers, there are no page errors and the relocated app still passes signature verification.
After the host is killed mid-installation, a reopened host reports nothing running, downloading or paused and the earlier runtime installed; the next request upgrades and then downloads.

cases.use: The app is force-quit while a model is loaded and a turn is running; on the next launch no leftover engine blocks the start and the conversation is intact.

tests.covers: SIGKILL of the real host while a scripted llama-server standing in for the loaded model streams a Chat turn: guard, server and relay exit, the engine port is free, and the relaunched host starts the model again and serves the conversation saved during the turn byte for byte.
